seating.note: Highest margin category — always include chairs in every proposal

reception.note: High margin, high brand impact — never let client under-invest here

boardroom.note: Strong margin, anchor piece for large projects

workstations.note: Volume category — margin protected by installation revenue

storage.note: Lower margin but builds order value and client dependency

anchoringStrategy.rule: Always present the premium configuration first. It frames the mid-range as 'value'.
anchoringStrategy.buyerBehaviour: 65–70% of buyers choose the middle option when presented with 3 tiers

priceRangesExGST.GOJOVol2: From $2,500+ per executive desk — ultra-premium positioning

upsellOpportunities.workstationToSitStand: $400–$600 per desk uplift — 60–70% acceptance when framed as a health investment
upsellOpportunities.deskToFullSuite: Add ergonomic chair, credenza, 2x visitor chairs, task lighting to every desk quote
upsellOpportunities.boardroomExtras: AV credenza, executive chairs, sideboard — never quote table alone
upsellOpportunities.receptionExtras: Lounge seating, coffee table, feature lighting — position as brand investment not furniture cost

projectExtrasMargin.deliveryInstallation: 15–25% of product value — always include in quotes above $20k
projectExtrasMargin.furnitureDisposal: If client has old furniture — charge for removal and disposal
projectExtrasMargin.floorPlanSignOff: Include as a value-add for projects above $80k

riskHighMarginScenarios: Interstate freight without proper loading — add margin buffer
Customer-supplied items mixing with TCD items — avoid or charge coordination fee
Under-specified projects with likely scope creep — add 15% contingency minimum

financeOptions.positioning: Position finance as a cash flow tool for CFOs — 'spread the investment across the asset life'
